function.name: bash
function.description: Run a shell command in the local working directory. Use for git, tests, installs, and one-off scripts. Do not use it to cat/sed/head/read/write/grep source files — use the read, write, edit, and grep tools instead. If stdout is longer than 2000 lines or 50KB, the full output is saved under tools_result/bash/ and this result is head+tail only — grep or read that saved path. Do not pipe head/tail yourself.

function.name: read
function.description: Read a file. Text files return numbered lines (offset 1-based, limit). pdf/docx/xlsx are extracted to text: short files return inline; long ones save under tools_result/read/ and return a preview — grep or read that saved path. Do not use bash to cat or parse these.

path.description: Path relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return

function.name: write
function.description: Create or overwrite a whole text file. Use for new files or full-file rewrites. Overwriting an existing file requires a prior read of that path; creating a new file does not. Do not use bash cat/heredoc for this. For a small in-place patch, use edit (old must be unique unless replace_all). Path is relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is). content is the full file text; empty string is allowed.

path.description: Path relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is)

content.description: Full file text to write. Empty string creates an empty file.

function.name: edit
function.description: Replace a snippet in an existing file. Read the file first (paginated reads count). old is exact text (not regex) copied from read without line numbers. old must appear exactly once unless replace_all is true. new may be empty to delete the snippet. Do not use this to create files — use write. Do not use bash sed for this.

path.description: Path relative to the workspace, or an absolute path (absolute is used as-is)

old.description: Exact text to find. Must be unique in the file unless replace_all is true. Cannot be empty.

new.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the snippet.

replace_all.description: If true, replace every occurrence of old. Default false.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents with a regex. Returns path:line:content. Optional path (file or directory, default workspace) and glob (e.g. *.py). Prefer this over bash grep. First page is 20 matches; if the footer includes cursor, call grep again with that cursor to get the next page. Do not use this to read whole files — use read.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for. Required unless cursor is set.

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the workspace.

glob.description: Only search files matching this glob, e.g. *.py or *.{ts,tsx}

cursor.description: Pagination token from a previous grep. Pass it to get the next page of the same search.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web for up-to-date information. Returns a ranked list of title, URL, and snippet. Prefer this over bash curl to search engines. If you need a specific page's full text, that is a later step — this tool only searches.

max_results.description: How many results to return (default 5, max 10)

function.name: web_fetch
function.description: Fetch a public http(s) URL. HTML becomes readable text; JSON and plain text stay as text. The full page is saved as UTF-8 under tools_result/web_fetch/: a `[web_fetch] url` header, then the body. It is not raw HTTP bytes and not guaranteed valid JSON. The tool result is a short preview plus the saved path — grep or read that path (set path= the file). Do not bash that file and do not json.load the whole file. Use when the user pastes a link or a search hit needs the page body. Fails for private/localhost URLs, login walls, PDFs, and JavaScript-only apps. Prefer this over bash curl.

url.description: The URL to fetch. http is upgraded to https.

function.name: memory_search
function.description: Search cross-session memory (project MEMORY.md, dated session notes, and global MEMORY.md). Use for prior decisions, how this repo is built, and user preferences. Do not use grep on the repo for that. Recalled memory is historical — verify against live files. Pass query to search; pass path (MEMORY.md, global/MEMORY.md, or a dated .md name) to read one file.

query.description: Keywords (AND). Omit when reading a file by path.

path.description: Short memory path: MEMORY.md, global/MEMORY.md, or YYYY-MM-DD-*.md

offset.description: When reading by path, 1-based start line

limit.description: When reading by path, max lines
